purpose: A synthetic ten-meeting corpus and the questions asked of it. Every word was invented for this file: no meeting recording, Preview datum, or product record appears in it. Both arms read this one file, so neither implementation carries its own copy of what the right answer is.
unit: One vector per meeting. The queue row asks for search over the corpus, which is a question about which meeting to open. Landing on the exact claim inside one is Wave 1 item 6 and needs a different unit, so it is not measured here.
keyword: The single word a person would type into today's exact search when trying to find this meeting. It is what the probe is measured against, because it is what the product already does.
exact_finds: Meeting IDs `library_read::search(keyword)` actually returns. Asserted by a Rust test against the real function, so the baseline cannot drift from the shipped one or be written down from memory.
shape: Five questions where the keyword already works and five where it does not. A suite of only the second kind rewards any non-empty retrieval; a suite of only the first measures nothing a substring search cannot already do.

turns: Right, the warehouse move. We are looking at the second week of April.
That gives the fulfilment team three weeks to run both sites in parallel.
Ravi wants the racking installed before the first pallet arrives.
The pricing page conversion has dropped every week since the redesign.
We changed the annual toggle to be the default and it has not helped.
I want to put the monthly option back on top and watch it for a fortnight.
Halloway are up for renewal at the end of the quarter.
Their usage is down about a third but they have added two new teams.
I think we hold the price and offer the onboarding sessions instead.
The schema migration went out last night and nobody looked at the reporting jobs.
Three of them are writing into a column that no longer exists.
I can roll the migration back but we lose the new audit fields.
Dana is taking over onboarding from the first of next month.
She wants two weeks of shadowing before she runs a session on her own.
We should tell the customers who already have sessions booked.
The Bristol pilot ends in three weeks and they have not signed anything.
Their finance team keeps asking for a breakdown we have already sent twice.
Either we extend it another month or we let it lapse quietly.
We are not shipping the Atlas migration this quarter.
The field team will be unhappy but the rollback plan is not written.
I would rather slip it than spend a weekend restoring from backups.
Two people have resigned from the support rota this month.
That leaves us with one person covering the overnight window.
We either pause overnight cover or we pay an agency to fill it.
The lease on this floor is up in September and the landlord wants a five year term.
Half the team has not come in more than once a week since January.
A smaller floor with better meeting rooms would suit us better.
The security review flagged the way we store the export files.
They are sitting in a bucket with no expiry and no access logging.
Adding a lifecycle rule is a day of work and closes the finding.

questions.question: When are we moving the warehouse?
questions.why: The word is in the meeting. A substring search already finds it and semantic must not lose it.

questions.question: What did we decide about the Halloway renewal?
questions.why: A proper noun, said aloud. Exact search is good at these and should stay the thing to beat.

questions.question: Who is taking over onboarding?
questions.why: The keyword appears in two meetings, so retrieval has to pick between them rather than merely find one.

questions.question: What is happening with the Bristol pilot?
questions.why: Another proper noun. Present so the suite is not only cases where exact search fails.

questions.question: Are we still shipping the Atlas migration?
questions.why: The word is there and so is the negation. Exact search wins; semantic must too.

questions.question: Which meeting was about hiring problems?
questions.why: Nobody said hiring. They said two people resigned and one person is covering nights.

questions.question: Did we talk about giving up some of our office space?
questions.why: The meeting is about a lease and a smaller floor. Neither the question's words nor its idea appear literally — the word office was in this transcript until it was removed, because a lexical control found the meeting through it.

questions.question: What was the data retention problem?
questions.why: The meeting says no expiry and no access logging. Retention is the concept, not the word.

questions.question: Where did the database change break something?
questions.why: The transcript says schema, migration and column, never database — and the word change was removed for the same reason office was, because the control matched on it.

questions.question: Why are fewer people buying the subscription?
questions.why: The meeting is about conversion on a pricing page and an annual toggle. The word is absent.
